lots.title: Multi-disciplinary Design Team Appointment — Stockport Town Centre School
lots.description: Appointment of an architecturally led multi-disciplinary design team to deliver feasibility through to concept design (RIBA Stage 2) of a new exemplar town-centre through-school in Stockport, supporting the Council's wider £1bn town-centre regeneration on a constrained, previously developed (brownfield) site. The briefing document does not subdivide scope into separately bidable lots; it describes a single architecturally-led consultant-team appointment with a unified multi-disciplinary scope (Architecture, M&E, Structures & Civils, BR PD and CDM PD). Procurement is run under a Competitive Flexible Procedure with a Stage 1 Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) shortlisting to top 3 suppliers, followed by Stage 2 detailed proposals.
requirements: Multi-disciplinary team comprising Architecture, M&E, Structures & Civils, BR PD (Building Regulations Principal Designer) and CDM PD (CDM Principal Designer) within a single architecturally-led consultant team.
Demonstrable experience of designing and delivering through-schools of similar size on complex, constrained, town and city-centre locations.
Inclusive design approach that meets the needs of all learners; flexible, adaptable spaces that can evolve with changing educational needs.
Embed green building standards, active travel promotion and adaptability; contribute to climate resilience (including flood risk) in line with the Council's 2019 climate emergency declaration.
Meet the Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) target of 20% for the site.
Navigate brownfield development constraints including high remediation costs, proximity to primary traffic routes with significant volumes, and air-quality impacts.
Navigate town-centre heritage / historic townscape sensitivities and complement the existing skyline and character.
Provide consistency at Partner level throughout the design programme (stated SMBC preference).

Report to the SMBC Project Board (Estates, Education, MDC) and supporting teams — Estates and Asset Management (EAM), Design and Technical Services, Education Services, Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation, Local Council Members, Local Planning Authority, Highways, Sustainability — at frequent intervals during the commission; agree stage-reporting dates with the Head of Capital Design & Technical Services.

Support a viable funding model for the Town Centre School project, including public funding streams, grants, phased delivery, partnerships and value-engineering approaches; integrate cost planning, risk management and lifecycle considerations into the design process.

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Relevant experience and contract examples (Stage 1 PSQ Q1)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Part 1: 500-word narrative describing experience of designing and delivering school projects on complex, constrained and urban sites — challenges encountered, how addressed, outcomes achieved. Part 2: three case studies, each with a separate 250-word narrative on relevance to Part 1 plus a separate single A4 sheet of case-study details (format at bidder discretion).
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Equally weighted with the other two Stage 1 PSQ questions (three equally weighted questions at Stage 1).

evaluation_criteria.summary: Part 1: name each member of the proposed multidisciplinary team (company/practice) covering Architecture, M&E, Structures & Civils, BR PD and CDM PD; describe proposed team structure, key roles and responsibilities (max 500 words) and explain how the team's skills and experience align to the project (max 1000 words). Part 2: single-A4 CV per discipline lead, maximum 5 CVs.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Equally weighted with the other two Stage 1 PSQ questions.

evaluation_criteria.summary: Max 500 words covering: (1) understanding of financial challenges and opportunities of delivering a school within a town-centre context; (2) how the bidder will work with the client team to explore, evaluate and refine funding options (public funding streams, grants, phased delivery, partnerships, value-engineering); (3) methodology for ensuring affordability, including integration of cost planning, risk management and lifecycle considerations into the design process.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Equally weighted with the other two Stage 1 PSQ questions.

evaluation_criteria.summary: The Council intends to shortlist the top 3 highest-scoring Suppliers from Stage 1 to be invited to Stage 2, reserving the right to increase or decrease the number of Suppliers invited to Stage 2 where appropriate and proportionate. Shortlisted suppliers receive the full tender pack for Stage 2 detailed proposals.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: The Council intends to shortlist the top 3 highest scoring Suppliers to be invited to participate in Stage 2.

evaluation_criteria.summary: The Stage 2 Tender will be evaluated on the basis of quality (60%), price (40%) and social value (20%). Note the stated percentages sum to 120% — the document does not reconcile this; treat the stated weightings as literal.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Quality 60% / Price 40% / Social Value 20% (as literally stated).

Programme reference: the indicative programme covers RIBA Stage 2 design (concept design); a wider strategic programme will be issued with the Stage 2 tender documents.
Required discipline in the multi-disciplinary team: CDM Principal Designer (Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015).
